CATEGORY: Adj. can be predicate; usually Adj. takes 很 (Grammar)
definition: An adjective can be the predicate without 是. Usually use 很 before an adjective when giving a plain description, unless another degree pattern is intended.

HER NOTES IN THIS CATEGORY (5 distinct):
2 | 是Adj.的 is to emphasize
2 | usually Adj. takes 很
1 | Adj. can be predicate
1 | “这个植物“ is not unclear, which one? Delete 是，Adj. can be predicate, without是
1 | instead of using “有……” structure, it is better to use short sentences: 学历很高

output.rule: An Adj. can be the predicate without 是. Usually an Adj. takes 很 for a plain description; 是Adj.的 is used to emphasize.
output.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: <adjective> is a plain description, so use it as the predicate without 是 and usually add 很.

examples.explanation: 你应该特别是小心 → 你应该特别小心: 小心 is an Adj. predicate, so it does not take 是.
第二个房子离购物中心近 → 第二个房子离购物中心很近: 近 is a plain description, so it usually takes 很.
孟母看出来孟子老是难过 → 孟母看出来孟子老是很难过: 难过 is a plain description, so it usually takes 很.
孟子是淘气的孩子 → 孟子很淘气: 淘气 can be the predicate; use 很淘气 rather than 是淘气的孩子.
有高的学历 → 学历很高: use a short sentence with the Adj. predicate, 学历很高.

output.not_an_error: Do not flag 是Adj.的 when the writer intends emphasis. Do not require 很 when another degree pattern, such as 特别, is used.
